description: Employees often face a conflict between productivity and adhering to cybersecurity policies, which can lead to decreased performance and increased stress. The emphasis an organization places on productivity versus cybersecurity influences how employees balance these responsibilities, with decisions often driven by habitual behavior rather than rational cost-benefit analyses. title: Developing Training Research to Improve Cyber Defense of Industrial Control Systems
description: Cyber-attacks on Industrial Control Systems (ICS) can be particularly severe, as they may manipulate sensor and control data to cause significant damage, as exemplified by the Stuxnet worm. Given the advanced nature of these attacks, current automated detection systems are insufficient, necessitating continued human involvement in ICS protection. We propose several training-based solutions to enhance the defense of these systems by better preparing human operators to identify and respond to such
headings: H1: Developing Training Research to Improve Cyber Defense of Industrial Control Systems

title: Exploring the Hybrid Space
description: As cyberspace becomes integral to military operations, terms like cyber power and cyber deterrence highlight its growing importance. Future military personnel will face increased complexity in joint operations where cyberspace is a key enabler. This paper proposes the Hybrid Space framework to better understand the interplay between cyberspace and the physical domain, addressing cognitive challenges and informing the development of effective education and training programs.Authors: Øyvind Jøsok,

title: Macrocognition Applied to the Hybrid Space: Team Environment, Functions and Processes in Cyber Operations
description: As military cyber operations become more integrated, effective team coordination is crucial. This paper expands on a macrocognitive model by introducing the Hybrid Space framework, which maps cognitive processes across cyber-physical and tactical-strategic dimensions. This framework aims to enhance understanding of environmental complexity and improve team performance in cyber contexts. The paper also discusses insights from cyber network defense exercises at the Norwegian Defence Cyber Academy
headings: H1: Macrocognition Applied to the Hybrid Space: Team Environment, Functions and Processes in Cyber Operations

title: Neurosecurity: Human Brain Electro-Optical Signals as MASINT

This shift suggests we are moving towards a reality where human thought may no longer be considered entirely private. headings: H1: Neurosecurity: Human Brain Electro-Optical Signals as MASINT

description: In August 2024, the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) co-sponsored ConnectCon, an interactive workshop that facilitated meaningful conversations and connections between researchers and practitioners on the topic of human-centered cybersecurity. title: Socio-technical communication: The hybrid space and the OLB model for science-based cyber education
description: Lessons from safety-critical sociotechnical systems, such as aviation and acute medical care, underscore the vital role of human factors and effective communication between human agents. Failures in communication have been linked to many fatal incidents in aviation, highlighting the need for cognitive engineering to enhance performance in both civilian and military domains. headings: H1: Socio-technical communication: The hybrid space and the OLB model for science-based cyber education

title: The Enduring Mystery of the Repeat Clickers
description: Repeat Clickers—individuals within an organization who consistently fall for phishing emails—pose a significant security risk. This behavior, affecting a persistent minority, may be driven by individual traits or an interaction between these traits and external factors such as culture or social engineering tactics. headings: H1: The Enduring Mystery of the Repeat Clickers

title: Understanding Online Information Operations: Development of an Influence Network for Scientific Inquiry Testing Environment (INSITE)

Effective countermeasures must be developed to respond quickly and anticipate future threats. A major challenge in creating these countermeasures is the lack of a sophisticated testing environment for evaluating detection tools and algorithms. headings: H1: Understanding Online Information Operations: Development of an Influence Network for Scientific Inquiry Testing Environment (INSITE)
